initialize.instructions: Craft Anything shows how software works, with evidence. Start with core_investigation_show and core_session_show. Open a target with core_target_open (absolute path), then use focused tools; ask for summaries first and page for detail. Only the Essentials toolset is listed at first: call list_toolsets and enable_toolset to add native, Android, web and other tools. Keep the investigation memory current (core_brief_write, core_plan_update, core_hypothesis_record, core_finding_record with evidence ids, core_handoff_write at the end of each turn). Cite evidence ids, separate observations from inferences, and record open questions as unknowns. Tools that run code or change a device need the user's approval. In Clean room (Deep mode off) only the tools that work from outside are listed: nothing inside a target is read, and a refused tool says how to turn Deep mode on.

Sessions live in memory for this run; at most 4 at a time.

args.description: Arguments the program gets when it is run.

core.description: Absolute path of a core dump to open with the program.

program.description: Absolute path of the program to load; omit for an empty session.

tools.name: native_gdb_session_begin
tools.title: Start a GDB session

tools.description: Run one GDB command line in a session (for example `info functions`, `disassemble main`, `break main`, `run`, `bt`, `info registers`, `x/16xb $sp`) and return its console output, the result (done, running, error, exit), stop events (reason, frame) and any program output, waiting up to timeout_seconds for a started run to stop. Commands can run the program, call its functions or use GDB's shell and Python, so this asks for consent.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the command (and a started run) to finish: 1–300, default 10.

tools.name: native_gdb_command_run
tools.title: GDB command

tools.description: Show one GDB session (or all when session_id is omitted): whether GDB is alive, the last known program state (not started, stopped, running, exited), the last stop event, and any output that arrived since the last command.
tools.name: native_gdb_session_show
tools.title: GDB session status

tools.description: End a GDB session: ask GDB to exit, then stop it and anything it started (including a program it is debugging).
tools.name: native_gdb_session_end
tools.title: Close a GDB session

tools.description: Start Rizin's debugger (user settings and scripts off, no prompt or colours) on a program (absolute path, optional arguments), which it starts stopped before its first instruction, or attach it to a running process by pid. Returns a session_id for native_rizin_session_command_run, native_rizin_session_show and native_rizin_session_end, plus Rizin's start-up messages. The program's own console output isn't captured. Sessions live in memory for this run; at most 4 at a time. Starting a program or attaching to one asks for consent.

pid.description: A running process to attach to instead of starting a program.

program.description: Absolute path of the program to start under the debugger.

tools.name: native_rizin_session_begin
tools.title: Start a Rizin debug session

tools.description: Run one Rizin command line in a debug session (for example `dr` registers, `db main` breakpoint, `dc` continue, `ds` step, `dbt` backtrace, `dm` memory maps, `pd 10 @ rip`, `px 64 @ rsp`; chain with `;`) and return its output and any `ERROR:` lines, waiting up to timeout_seconds. A command still running at the deadline (a `dc` that never stops) keeps running and the next command waits for it. Visual mode isn't available. Commands can run the program and change its memory, so this asks for consent.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the command to finish: 1–300, default 10.

tools.name: native_rizin_session_command_run
tools.title: Rizin debug command

tools.description: Show one Rizin debug session (or all when session_id is omitted): whether Rizin is alive, what it debugs, whether a command is still running, and any output that arrived since the last command.
tools.name: native_rizin_session_show
tools.title: Rizin debug session status

tools.description: End a Rizin debug session: ask Rizin to quit (which ends a program it started; an attached process is detached), then stop it and anything it started.
tools.name: native_rizin_session_end
tools.title: Close a Rizin debug session

tools.description: Decode a saved radio recording (absolute path or the active target) with rtl_433: I/Q samples (.cu8, .cs8, .cs16, .cf32) or demodulated AM/FM (.am.s16, .fm.s16), format and sample rate read from the file name (for example g001_433.92M_250k.cu8; 250 kHz when absent) unless sample_rate is given. Returns each decoded message (device model, id, channel and readings) paged with offset/limit, plus counts by model. decoders limits decoding to those protocol numbers (see radio_decoders_list); otherwise rtl_433's default set runs. Optional engine.

decoders.description: Protocol numbers to decode (from radio_decoders_list); empty runs the default set.

path.description: Absolute path of the recording; omit to use the active target.

sample_rate.description: Sample rate in Hz, when the file name doesn't say.

tools.name: radio_recording_decode
tools.title: Decode a radio recording

tools.description: List the device protocols the installed rtl_433 can decode: number, name, and whether it runs by default (the others only run when asked for with decoders). Optional engine.

filter.description: Only decoders whose name contains this text (any case).

tools.name: radio_decoders_list
tools.title: List radio decoders

tools.description: Find Cutter (or Rizin) sessions shared on this computer: each port given (default 9090) is asked what it has open (file, format, architecture). A session is shared by running `=h& 9090` in Cutter's console; nothing else is reachable.
tools.name: native_cutter_sessions_list
tools.title: List shared Cutter sessions

tools.description: Run one read-only Rizin command in a shared Cutter session (port, default 9090) and return its text, paged by lines: information (i…), printing and disassembly (p…, x…), analysis (a…), search (/…), seek (s…), flags (f…), comments (C…), types (t…) and help (?…). Writes, shell escapes, scripts, debugging, pipes and chaining are refused. Analysis and seek commands change what the Cutter window shows, as if typed in its console.

command.description: One read-only Rizin command, for example `afl`, `pdf @ main` or `iz`.

offset.description: First output line of the page.

tools.name: native_cutter_command_run
tools.title: Cutter command

tools.description: Decompile a Java .class file or JAR (absolute path or the active target) to Java source with Vineflower, run as a program (its .jar with the configured Java, or a vineflower script; set its path in Settings → Engines). Without class: the decompiled source files with their line counts, paged with offset/limit (and the source itself when there is one file). With class (com.example.Foo or com/example/Foo): that class's source, paged by lines; inner classes are inside their outer class's file. Optional engine.

class.description: One class to show (com.example.Foo or com/example/Foo).

limit.description: Files or lines per page (1–20000, default 2000).

offset.description: First file (or, with class, first line) of the page.

path.description: Absolute path of a .class or .jar; omit to use the active target.

tools.name: java_vineflower_decompile
tools.title: Decompile Java with Vineflower
